question: Which forms does the Lord name as his own among peoples and sages?
premises: The Lord names Vāsudeva among the Vṛṣṇis.
The Lord names Dhanañjaya among the Pāṇḍavas.
The Lord names Vyāsa among sages and Uśanas among poets.
inference: The verse lists representative divine manifestations among named groups.
uncertainties: The fused token munīnāmapyahaṃ is glossed as a whole, not split.
plain_english: Among the Vṛṣṇis I am Vāsudeva; among the Pāṇḍavas, Dhanañjaya; among sages, Vyāsa; among poets, Uśanas the poet.
